newsitem.title: JORDAN: Accused schoolgirls killer ousted from Jordan trial.
newsitem.headline: Accused schoolgirls killer ousted from Jordan trial.

text.p: A Jordanian soldier charged with premeditated murder of seven Israeli schoolgirls was thrown out of his own military trial on Wednesday for shouting down a prosecution witness.

Private Ahmed al-Daqamsa, who has not denied gunning down the Israelis near a border post three months ago, scuffled with six military policemen and was bundled out of court after he challenged testimony from one of his army comrades.
"Lie!" shouted Daqamsa when Corporal Youssef Mahmoud told the five-man military tribunal where Daqamsa's colleagues were shortly before the shooting.
"I'm not going out!" he retorted when tribunal head Brigadier Mamoun al-Khasawneh ordered him out of the courtroom.
Daqamsa, gripping the black bars of his cage inside the dock, refused to leave. Military police piled into the cage, kicked him and dragged him out, while his family screamed and shouted.
Two of Daqamsa's relatives were also thrown out.
Daqamsa was allowed back into court 20 minutes after his display of defiance. Head bowed, he remained silent for the remaining four hours of testimony.
"He's facing the death penalty. It's not surprising that he should be agitated," chief defence lawyer Hussein Majalli said.

Witnesses said Daqamsa shot the Israeli girls, six of them 13 years old and one just 11 years old, in the Jordanian border territory of Baqoura leased to Israel under a 1994 peace treaty. They said he fired off nearly three ammunition clips of 30 bullets each before his rifle jammed.
Under the peace accord Jordanian soldiers patrol the area but Israelis have free access and Israelis farmers own land there. Israelis call it 'The Island of Peace'.
King Hussein said Daqamsa's action had shamed the army and he should have been shot dead on the spot, but Jordan's vocal opponents of the peace treaty have rallied to his defence.

His 92-member defence committee is led by Majalli, head of Jordan's lawyers union. Former Prime Minister Ahmed Obeidat, a fierce critic of the peace accord, and engineers union boss Laith Shubailat have both attended court sessions.

Daqamsa, 26, from a small town in northern Jordan, has been portrayed by his defence as a pious man with a burning resentment against Israel who shot the girls in a fit of rage because they teased him.
The prosecution has called witnesses who said Daqamsa rarely prayed, talked about sex so much he was called Ahmed Sex in his army unit, and plotted for years to kill Israelis.

"Hey Sex, you've got no principles," Sergeant Salah Ahmed said when he saw Daqamsa praying an hour and a half before the shooting. When the Israeli girls arrived, he said Daqamsa told him to look at their "beautiful white flesh".
Another soldier, Corporal Mohammad Abdullah, said Daqamsa told him a few hours before the shooting: "Today you're going to see something you've never seen before."
"You're all cowards. You should all do (what I did)," Abdullah quoted Daqamsa as saying after he shot the girls and was taken to army barracks.
